title: Pasqal Transitions €50 Million Q-PLANET Pilot Line into Execution Phase for European Neutral-Atom Chips - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Pasqal (NASDAQ: PSQL) says the EU Chips JU-backed Q-PLANET pilot line, a EUR 50M, three-year, 28-partner, 11-country project, has entered its execution phase to build a European semiconductor and photonic supply chain for neutral-atom quantum computing, sensing and communications.

insights.claim: Pasqal leads the 28-partner, 11-country Q-PLANET consortium, which moved into its execution phase three months after the Brussels kick-off.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A tangible EU industrial-policy vehicle for neutral-atom hardware with Pasqal as coordinator.

insights.claim: Q-PLANET is co-funded with EUR 50 million (about $57.2M) over three years by the EU Chips JU plus national and regional agencies including France 2030, ERDF, Business Finland, FFG and the Baden-Württemberg science ministry.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Public money de-risks Pasqal’s supply-chain build; the amount is small versus typical fab capex.

insights.claim: Deliverables include integrated chip-based laser sources at 461, 698, 795 and 1013 nm, atom chips for processors and sensors, microfabricated vapor cells for atomic clocks, and standardized Process Design Kits (PDKs) and Assembly Design Kits (ADKs) for commercial foundries.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PDKs/ADKs are the step that lets foundries manufacture quantum components, a precondition for scaling neutral-atom QPUs.

insights.claim: Pasqal directly leads the 1013 nm laser stream and acts as end-user validator for the vapor cells and laser sources integrated in its neutral-atom QPUs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Pasqal secures first access to subsidized components for its own roadmap.
insights.locator: Pasqal serves as both lead project coordinator

insights.claim: Transitioning lab-scale photonic and vapor-cell prototyping to commercial semiconductor fabrication lines is the central aim, supporting a domestic European supply chain for neutral-atom computing, sensing and communications.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Part of Europe’s sovereignty push in quantum supply chains; compare with US efforts such as Infleqtion’s foundry work.
insights.locator: to construct a domestic semiconductor and photonic supply chain

insights.claim: The standardized processes are meant to support upcoming European quantum infrastructure deployments at HPC centers (TGCC, Forschungszentrum Jülich, CINECA) and commercial uses such as drug discovery and advanced materials.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: HPC-center installs are the near-term demand for Pasqal QPUs; commercial use cases remain prospective.
insights.locator: The initiative establishes standardized manufacturing processes
